\noindent{\Large\textbf{Presentation grading sheet}}\hfill Research Design and Methods in Quantitative Research, Fall 2026\\[8pt]
\noindent Session: \rule{1.8cm}{0.4pt}\quad Date: \rule{2.6cm}{0.4pt}\quad Presenter(s): \rule{15cm}{0.4pt}\\[8pt]

\noindent Score each criterion from 0 to 5 points. The descriptions show what earns 5, 3 and 1 points; 4 and 2 lie in between, and 0 means the criterion was not addressed.\\[4pt]
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\noindent\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.4cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\centering\arraybackslash}p{1.5cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Criterion} & \textbf{5 points} & \textbf{3 points} & \textbf{1 point} & \textbf{Score}\\
\midrule
\textbf{Clarity} & Follows the two-part structure, uses uncluttered slides with visual aids, and finishes within 25 minutes. & Mostly easy to follow, but some slides are overcrowded, transitions are unclear, or the timing is off. & Hard to follow: text-heavy slides, a part is missing, or the time limit is clearly exceeded. & \\[1.2em]
\midrule
\textbf{Understanding} & Accurately presents the argument, research question, hypotheses, method, data, unit of analysis and key findings, and links the design to the paper's goal. & Mostly accurate, but some elements of the design are missing or treated superficially. & Misrepresents the paper or leaves out core elements of its design. & \\[1.2em]
\midrule
\textbf{Critique quality} & Names specific strengths and the main limitations of the design (e.g., measurement, validity, scope) and stays constructive. & Identifies limitations, but they are generic, minor or one-sided. & The critique is missing, superficial or merely dismissive. & \\[1.2em]
\midrule
\textbf{Reasoning} & Focuses on one key limitation, justifies why it matters, and derives the proposal from it step by step. & The link between critique and proposal is there, but partly implicit or weakly justified. & The proposal is unrelated to the critique or not justified. & \\[1.2em]
\midrule
\textbf{Feasibility} & Proposes a concrete, realistic design (data, cases, empirical strategy) that would address the limitation. & The design is plausible but vague on data or method, or partly unrealistic. & The proposal is unrealistic or is not a research design. & \\[1.2em]
\midrule
\textbf{Discussion} & Answers questions accurately, takes up critique, and uses it to improve the proposal. & Answers most questions, but engages little with the feedback. & Struggles to answer questions or dismisses the feedback. & \\[1.2em]

\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}\\[8pt]
\noindent\textbf{Total:} \rule{1.5cm}{0.4pt} / 30 points \qquad \textbf{Grade:} \rule{1.5cm}{0.4pt} \qquad 15 points = 4.0 (pass), 30 = 6.0, linear in between; rounded to half grades; below 15 never a pass. Pairs: same grade.\\[6pt]
